haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 minutes). If not claimed, an expiry job runs every minute, marks the hold EXPIRED and returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge, and payment is requested only after StockReserved. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the order becomes REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses idempotency key = order id. Retries after a timeout reuse the same key, so the provider returns the original result instead of charging again.
haiku-low.q4: The order is set to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with refund PENDING. A full refund is requested via RefundRequested, the customer is emailed, and the refund ends REFUNDED or STUCK.
haiku-low.q5: Only when OrderConfirmed is emitted, and it removes only the order's snapshot lines. On checkout failure the cart is left exactly as it was and the customer can retry.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service coordinates checkout and owns the order's status. Its progress record is the order status stored with the orders.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies it, stores the event and updates the payment. Payment then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker for Order.
haiku-low.q8: The provider event id is unique in webhook_events. A repeat is acknowledged with 200 OK and not processed. Consumers also keep inbox tables of handled event ids and ignore repeats.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and emits ReleaseStock when PaymentDeclined arrives. Inventory frees the hold at once rather than waiting out the 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: At claim time Inventory decides. If the hold is HELD, or EXPIRED with every line still free, the claim succeeds and the order is fulfilled. Otherwise the claim fails and the order is cancelled and refunded.
haiku-low.q11: The refund record is never deleted. Each failure adds 1 attempt and sets a backoff retry time; a worker retries with the same key refund-<order id>. After the limit it becomes STUCK and ops is alerted. Tracked in Payment's refunds.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event causes the Cart service to empty the cart. It removes only the lines in the order's snapshot.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 minutes). If not claimed, the expiry job (runs every minute) marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale. An EXPIRED hold can still be claimed if every line is still free at claim time.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging (order first, then reserve, then pay). If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all or nothing), StockShort lists the short items, no payment is requested, and the order becomes REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK with the items shown to the customer.
sonnet.q3: The charge is sent with an idempotency key equal to the order id, and retries use the same key, so the provider returns the original result.
sonnet.q4: The claim fails (StockClaimFailed), so the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with refund status PENDING. The customer is emailed that a full refund is on its way, and RefundRequested is emitted for the full amount. The refund goes to REFUNDED or STUCK.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when OrderConfirmed is emitted (on success), and only the snapshot lines are removed. On any failure the cart is left exactly as it was and the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: The Order service coordinates and decides the next step after each event. The record is the order's status (PLACED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, etc.) stored in Order, plus the refund status.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies the signature, stores it, and emits PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as an event on the broker. Order consumes that event.
sonnet.q8: Payment checks the provider event id against the unique webhook_events table. A duplicate is acknowledged with 200 and not processed, so no event is emitted twice. Consumers also keep an inbox of handled event ids and ignore repeats, and Order applies an event only if the current status allows it.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released at once (reservation becomes RELEASED, stock back on sale). PaymentDeclined makes Order set PAYMENT_DECLINED and emit ReleaseStock, which Inventory consumes.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim (ClaimStock) and Inventory decides in a single transaction. If the hold is EXPIRED but every line is still free right now, the claim succeeds and the order is confirmed. If the stock has gone to someone else (or the hold was RELEASED), the claim fails and the order is cancelled with a full refund.
sonnet.q11: The refund record is kept, set to FAILED, attempts is increased by 1, and a next retry time is set with backoff. A worker retries when due with the same key (refund-<order id>). After the retry limit it becomes STUCK, RefundStuck is emitted, and an ops alert is raised. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table (one per order), and the customer sees the refund as pending until REFUNDED or STUCK. Order also holds the refund status.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event causes it, and the Cart service does the clearing (removing only the lines in the order's snapshot).
